result.label: feature
result.what_to_change: slugify() uses NFKD normalization plus a `[^a-z0-9]+` replacement, which works for accented Latin (NFKD splits them into base Latin letter + combining accent, which gets stripped) but destroys non-Latin scripts like Greek or Cyrillic entirely, since those letters have no Latin decomposition and get replaced along with everything else. To keep Greek/Cyrillic report names in export filenames (used by formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts), slugify needs to preserve non-Latin letter characters (e.g. matching against a broader Unicode letter/number class such as \p{L}\p{N} instead of a[-z0-9] only) rather than stripping anything outside ASCII.
result.evidence: src/util/strings.ts: slugify() comment says 'Accents are dropped, not transliterated' and the regex `.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")` strips any character outside ASCII a-z0-9, which removes Greek/Cyrillic letters entirely (they have no Latin base after NFKD decomposition), while accented Latin letters decompose to a plain ASCII letter plus a combining mark that gets filtered. This function is used by formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts to build the export file name from report.name, matching the issue's symptom exactly: accented Latin keeps its letters, non-Latin scripts lose everything, falling back to 'report-<date>'.

not_searched: src/api/reports.ts and src/export/scheduler.ts in detail (only confirmed they call formatExportFilename)
test/exportUtils.test.ts full contents

input.title: Preserve non-Latin letters (Greek/Cyrillic) in slugify for export filenames
input.body:
File: src/util/strings.ts

slugify() currently normalizes with NFKD and strips anything matching `[^a-z0-9]+`, which only preserves Latin letters (accented Latin decomposes to ASCII + combining marks that get removed) while destroying Greek, Cyrillic, and other non-Latin scripts entirely. Update the replacement to use a broader Unicode-aware character class (e.g. `\p{L}\p{N}` with the `u` flag) instead of ASCII-only `a-z0-9`, so report names in non-Latin scripts are preserved in export filenames generated by formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts.

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/exportUtils.ts

formatExportFilename() computes the date suffix via at.toISOString().slice(0,10), which converts to UTC before slicing, so an evening export in a time zone behind UTC (e.g. Los Angeles) gets stamped with the next day's date. It should use the exporting user's local date instead.

input.body:
label: feature
file: src/util/strings.ts

slugify() uses NFKD normalization plus a `[^a-z0-9]+` replacement, which strips any non-Latin letters (Greek, Cyrillic, etc.) entirely while preserving accented Latin letters (which decompose to an ASCII base letter). This affects export filenames generated via formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts, causing non-Latin report names to fall back to a generic "report-<date>" filename.
